title: The Geyser That Keeps Time
subject: English
source: Written for english/y4 lesson 98 (Year 4 end-of-year reading paper: 'The Geyser That Keeps Time' (an original passage about Old Faithful in Yellowstone, with 15 questions; written for this assessment; in the portal and printable))
intro: Lesson 98. Read the passage carefully, then answer every question.

passage.title: The Geyser That Keeps Time
paras: Yellowstone National Park lies mostly in the state of Wyoming, in the United States. It was the first national park in the world, set up in 1872. Visitors come to see bison, bears and wolves, but many come for something even stranger: water that shoots out of the ground.

Deep under Yellowstone is a huge store of hot, melted rock. It heats water that has soaked down through cracks in the ground. The water becomes hotter and hotter, until it turns to steam and bursts upwards through a narrow hole. This is called a geyser.

Yellowstone has hundreds of geysers, but the most famous is Old Faithful. It got its name in 1870, when explorers noticed that it erupted again and again, as if keeping time. Today it erupts about every 60 to 110 minutes, sending boiling water up to 55 metres into the air. Each eruption lasts between one and a half and five minutes.

Rangers can even predict the next eruption. They time how long each one lasts: a long eruption is usually followed by a longer wait. A board in the visitor centre shows when to gather on the wooden walkway.
The walkways are there for a reason. The ground near the geysers can be thin, and the water beneath is boiling. Visitors must stay on the paths, so that both they and the geysers stay safe.

questions.q: In which state is Yellowstone mostly found?
Name two animals visitors come to see.
What heats the water under Yellowstone?
questions.a: A huge store of hot, melted rock
Hot water and steam bursting upwards through a narrow hole in the ground

questions.q: When did Old Faithful get its name?
How often does Old Faithful erupt?
How high can the water go?
How long does each eruption last?
questions.a: Between one and a half and five minutes

questions.q: How do rangers predict the next eruption?
questions.a: They time each eruption; a long one is followed by a longer wait

questions.q: Why is it called Old Faithful?
questions.a: It erupts again and again, regularly, as if keeping time

questions.q: Find a word that means 'to say what will happen'.
Why must visitors stay on the walkways? Give two reasons.
questions.a: The ground can be thin; the water beneath is boiling (and to protect the geysers)

questions.q: What does 'as if keeping time' suggest about the geyser?
questions.a: It is regular and reliable, like a clock

questions.q: Summarise the passage in one sentence.
questions.a: Yellowstone's geysers, especially the regular Old Faithful, shoot boiling water into the air and must be visited safely.
